newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Vranitzky says wins compromise in Albania crisis.
newsitem.headline: Vranitzky says wins compromise in Albania crisis.

text.p: European envoy Franz Vranitzky said on Thursday he had persuaded Albanian political parties to compromise over new elections, a move widely seen as vital to avert fresh crisis in the Balkan state.
Vranitzky told a news conference he had convinced the parties to amend a new electoral law, which had caused most political parties to threaten to boycott the planned elections.

The early elections, planned for the end of June, are seen as they key to stopping Albania sliding once again into the violence of February and March which came after the collapse of dubious investment schemes.
But most parties threatened to boycott the poll after the Democratic Party of President Sali Berisha forced a law through parliament which the parties said favoured Berisha.

Vranitzky said he won an agreement to amend the law, which would be brought back to parliament on Thursday evening. He also said that an election law prepared by an interim Government of National Reconciliation would also be discussed.

Vranitzky warned that if a compromise was not reached then the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), the Council of Europe and other international bodies would reconsider their commitment to monitor the elections, vital for them to be considered as free and fair.
